newsitem.title: POLAND: BBL cleared to up Amerbank stake.
newsitem.headline: BBL cleared to up Amerbank stake.

text.p: The National Bank of Poland, the country's central bank, has cleared Belgium's Banque Bruxelles Lambert's buy of (BBL) a 20 percent stake in Polish bank Amerbank SA, Amerbank said in a statement on Wednesday.
BBL currently has five-percent control of Amerbank.

Amerbank deputy president Wlodzimierz Paszkowski told Reuters on Wednesday that it could take up to six weeks to determine whether BBL would buy shares from current shareholders or take part in Amerbank's planned share issue.
The issue of 1.5 million shares is scheduled from May 5 to May 12.
"We are interested in having a foreign active banking partner which would channel some of its clients, some of its know-how...but still with a minority shareholding," Paszkowski said.
BBL would be better able to service its clients in Poland, Paszkowski said.
The move still needs to be approved by the Polish Securities Commission (KPW).
Paszkowski said the potential share sales by current investors would take place through the Warsaw bourse's kerb.
Oil and gas firm Polskie Gornictwo Naftowe i Gazownictwo is currently Amerbank's largest shareholder, with 24 percent.

Paszkowski said Morrison Knudsen Corp, which controls 17 percent of the bank, might sell some of its shares, as might HAC, an investment arm of Bankers Trust, which has 7.8 percent. Some of the shares of such stockholders would have to be converted into common shares from preferred shares, which are more heavily weighted than common shares.
He said Time Warner, which holds less than five percent of the bank, might also sell shares.
Amerbank currently has 2.7 million shares outstanding.
